_comment: CANCELLATION / FAILED PAYMENT — the other half of the answer, and the half that is easy to skip.
This experiment asks whether people will pay for a recurring plan. A signup that cancels in week two
is a different answer than one that renews, and Mixpanel cannot see either — cancellation happens in
Stripe's hosted portal, which this page deliberately does not wrap. Without this card, the only
number anyone reports is gross signups, which is the flattering one.
Add it as a second branch on the same flow (or a second flow) for customer.subscription.deleted and
invoice.payment_failed. Same verify-then-read discipline as the signup card: every expression reads
the RE-FETCHED event, never triggerBody(). See docs/stripe-webhook.md.
For customer.subscription.deleted that object is a Subscription; for invoice.payment_failed it is an
Invoice. The fields used below exist on both, which is why the two events can share one card.

facts._comment: A cancellation inside the first cycle is the signal worth chasing — it usually means the plan was not what they thought they were buying, which is a page problem, not a billing problem.
facts.title: Next
facts.value: Stop the manual coupon so bookings are not zeroed out any more, and log WHY. A first-cycle cancellation is feedback on the offer — ask before closing it out.
